rationale: Fix-up diff reviewed against the recorded baseline (backend 455e77355, frontend 645595689): 11 backend files, 2 frontend files. CR-001 — the settings handler now resolves the same merged per-slot view as the service, and a new test asserts an assistant-scoped slot survives an unrelated workflow row; the previously untested branch is covered. CR-002 — superseded by a product decision: 'None' means no selection, so at workflow scope it drops the override and inheritance resumes; the behaviour is now pinned by test_clearing_a_slot_in_workflow_scope_returns_to_inheritance rather than changed. CR-003 — the panel tracks changed slots and sends only those in workflow scope; verified by mutation (disabling the filter fails the new test). CR-004/CR-005 — the checkbox default now aggregates the orchestrator and every sub-assistant and is resolved even when the orchestrator has no slots of its own; also mutation-verified. CR-006 — the flag is bool(row and row.tools_config) on both the service and the GET branch, covered by a new empty-row test. CR-007 — downgrade archives workflow-scoped rows into assistant_user_mapping_workflow_scope_backup before deleting and its predicate now also catches NULL. CR-008 — promote_to_assistant_scope performs the upsert and the delete in one session and commit. CR-009 — the repository scope tests assert bound parameters and were mutation-verified (breaking the default fails them). No new high-risk issue appeared in the fix-up, so the narrow confirmation pass was not needed. Confidence is medium rather than high because the alembic migration still cannot be exercised by the suite (DB engine globally mocked) and manual verification against a local Postgres is outstanding.
